newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS END BARELY LOWER, EARLY GAINS ERASED.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS END BARELY LOWER, EARLY GAINS ERASED.

text.p: Seoul stocks finished barely lower on consolidation on Wednesday as profit-takers wiped out earlier gains near the close, brokers said.
"The market failed to keep its strength as strong selling pressure between 760-780 weighed it down," said Nah Dong-ik of Daishin Securities.
Brokers expected the battle to continue on Thursday, making it difficult for the market to rise to 770.
The composite stock index closed down 0.19 points to 762.73 with 33.4 million shares changing hands.
Losers overwhelmed gainers 514 to 276.
Prime blue chips outperformed the dull market, with Samsung Electronics leading the pack.
Brokers said the expectation that the foreign stock ownership ceiling would be expanded in the near future prompted active buying from foreign investors.
Samsung Electronics rose 2,200 won to 74,700, Pohang Iron and Steel added 500 to 61,900 and SK Telecom climbed 8,000 to 503,000.
"Blue chips are expected to stay firm for another day, supported by strong buying from institutions and foreigners," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities.
Brokers said stocks that investors expected to post improved first-half earnings fared well.

Hyundai Wood Industry, South Korea's largest integrated manufacturer of wood products, surged 590 won to end at its limit high of 7,980. Cambridge Members, a maker of men's suits, also hit its upper limit of 18,700, rising 1,300.
LG Electronics, which announced strong first-half earnings in the morning, closed up 400 to 19,400. LG posted a net profit of 109.6 billion won from 78.3 billion a year ago.
Daewoo Electronics lost 100 to 7,950 as its earnings took a fall.
"Corporate results are directing share price movement," said Hwang of LG. "But the impact will be short-lived as shares had already moved on expectations."
Brokers said securities shares, which had risen earlier this week, fell prey to profit-takers. Its sub-index dropped 1.96 percent to 1,310.51.
Dainong Corp and Midopa were also hit by a report that the troubled Dainong Group had asked its prime bank, SEOULBANK, for urgent help.
The report could not be confirmed by Dainong officials.
Four Dainong units, including Dainong and Midopa, have been put under protection by banks from defaulting on debt payments.
Dainong closed down 160 won to 2,370 after briefly hitting its limit low of 2,330 in early morning and Midopa shed 410 to 6,500 after falling to its lower limit of 6,360.
"Dainong and Midopa shares will remain weak for the time being on their bleak future," said Hwang of LG. -- JEAN YOON (822) 727 5643
